title: Test data: generating it, anonymising it and reusing it

videos.script: Every test needs data before it can start. An account to book with, a show with seats, an order in the right state. {{needs}} Where that data comes from decides whether you can trust the result. {{trust}} You can type it by hand. That is right for the few values a technique chooses. {{hand}} You can let a short program invent it, the same way every time. In this lesson, one signs up five accounts in boxoffice in a second. {{generate}} Or you can copy it from production, which has every odd case real customers ever made. It also has their names and their addresses. {{production}} So a copy is masked or pseudonymised first, and the law cares how it is done. {{law}} And whatever the source, a test has to start from the same state every time. Run the same program twice, and the second run fails with nothing wrong in the product. {{twice}} By the end of this lesson you know why, and how to get back to the start. {{reset}}
